scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

The sister is 21 years old, in her third year of university, and working to pay for her education. She's in business school, which she finds challenging but manageable. She's been saving money from her paychecks for a big vacation after she graduates, which is in about two years. The vacation fund has $2,800 in it, and she's planning to go on a cruise or visit places like Japan or Europe. Her brother is 30 years old, living with their parents, and is in a tough job while trying to go back to school to improve his situation. He's been living with their parents for about a year and a half. He hasn't been on a vacation in many years and has hinted that he needs one. Their parents have been helping him financially, but he didn't ask them for more help for this vacation. Instead, they suggested that he could have been saving money like the sister has, or start saving now to afford a trip in a year. Three days ago, the brother approached the sister and asked to borrow her vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or fall. He argued that since she won't need the money for another two years, he would have plenty of time to pay her back. The sister refused, citing her brother's poor money management skills and her discomfort with him being able to pay her back in time. The brother is upset, feeling it's unfair that the sister gets to go on more trips with their parents while he had to focus on college or work earlier in life. He also points out that the sister knew what she wanted to do for university right away, whereas he had to go back to school later. He even accuses her of being spoiled by their parents, which she disagrees with, stating that her ability to save is due to her father and her university classes teaching her to budget. The sister feels it's unfair to have to give up her vacation money to her brother, especially since she doubts his ability to pay her back on time. She's uncomfortable with the situation and is questioning whether she's being unreasonable (AITA - Am I The Asshole). Alright, so to determine whether it's right or wrong for the sister to refuse the loan, I need to consider several factors: 1. **Financial Responsibility:** The sister has been saving diligently for her future vacation, which is a responsible financial decision. She's planning for her future and has set aside money specifically for that purpose. 2. **Brother's Financial Situation:** The brother is in a difficult job and is trying to improve his situation by going back to school. He's living with their parents, which might limit his ability to save money. However, he's also been helped financially by their parents, which might mean he has some support system in place. 3. **Ability to Repay:** The sister is concerned about her brother's ability to repay the loan, given his history of being "horrible with money." This is a valid concern because if he can't repay, it could cause financial strain for her. 4. **Fairness and Equality:** The brother feels it's unfair that the sister gets to go on more trips with their parents while he had to focus on work and school. He also points out that she knew what she wanted to do for university right away, whereas he had to go back later. This sense of unfairness might be influencing his request. 5. **Parental Influence:** The parents suggested that the brother could have been saving like the sister or start saving now. This implies that they believe he has the means to save for his own vacation, which might make the sister's refusal seem more justified. 6. **Emotional Impact:** The sister is uncomfortable with the situation, and the brother is upset. This emotional tension could affect their relationship, which is an important factor to consider. 7. **Long-term Consequences:** If the sister lends her brother the money and he can't repay, it could strain their relationship and affect her ability to go on her planned vacation. On the other hand, refusing might lead to resentment from the brother. 8. **Alternative Solutions:** Instead of borrowing money, the brother could look for ways to earn extra income or find cheaper vacation options. The sister could also suggest these alternatives to help him without jeopardizing her own plans. Considering all these factors, it seems that the sister's decision to refuse the loan is reasonable. She has a valid concern about her brother's ability to repay, and she has been responsible with her savings. However, it's also important for her to communicate her reasons clearly and perhaps suggest alternative ways for her brother to achieve his goal without jeopardizing her own plans. Additionally, the brother's feelings of unfairness are understandable, but it's important for him to take responsibility for his financial situation and work towards improving it, rather than relying on his sister's savings. The parents' suggestion that he could have been saving like his sister indicates that they believe he has the capacity to do so, which further supports the sister's decision. In conclusion, while the sister's refusal might seem harsh, it is a responsible decision given her brother's financial habits and the potential risks involved. It's also an opportunity for both siblings to have a conversation about financial responsibility and support in a constructive manner.
